_notes.about: Copy this file to TaskDash.config.json and edit the copy. Keys that start with an underscore are ignored. Minimum config: set arcgis.url, keep arcgis.profile, and leave arcgis.item_id, arcgis.view_item_id and arcgis.dashboard_id empty; taskdash setup --apply fills those three. Every other key is optional. The notes below come in three groups: keys you set, keys that setup fills, and optional keys.
_notes._1_keys_you_set: Group 1. Keys you set. Every new install needs these.
_notes.arcgis.url: Your ArcGIS Online organization address, such as https://myorg.maps.arcgis.com; empty means www.arcgis.com. ArcGIS Enterprise is not tested.
_notes.arcgis.profile: Name of a saved ArcGIS sign-in profile; this keeps the password out of the file. Not the same as rules.profiles, which names rules files.
_notes.rules.profiles: Rules files added to rules/default.json, such as rules/your-org.json; an empty list uses only the default. Not the same as arcgis.profile, which names a sign-in.
_notes._2_keys_setup_fills: Group 2. Keys that taskdash setup --apply fills. Leave them empty.
_notes.arcgis.item_id: Item ID of the hosted table service the collector writes to. Leave empty: taskdash setup --apply fills it.
_notes.arcgis.view_item_id: Item ID of the read-only view the dashboard reads. Leave empty: taskdash setup --apply fills it.
_notes.arcgis.dashboard_id: Item ID of the dashboard. Leave empty: taskdash setup --apply fills it. taskdash dashboard --target prod updates this item.
_notes._3_optional_keys: Group 3. Optional keys. Each has a default. The last three are for development or deprecated; leave them empty.
_notes.host_name_override: Leave empty. TaskDash then uses the computer name. After a rename, use host_previous_names instead.
_notes.host_previous_names: Earlier names of this computer. Each collect --apply moves their inventory rows to the current name. Use it for one run after a rename, then empty it.
_notes.powershell_timeout_seconds: Seconds to wait for each PowerShell call before it is stopped.
_notes.arcgis.username: Sign-in name; leave empty when you use a profile or environment variables.
_notes.arcgis.password: Leave empty. A password here needs arcgis.allow_plaintext_password set to true.
_notes.arcgis.username_env: Name of an environment variable that holds the sign-in name.
_notes.arcgis.password_env: Name of an environment variable that holds the password.
_notes.arcgis.allow_plaintext_password: Set true only to accept a password stored in this file.
_notes.arcgis.service_description: Description text for the hosted service; empty uses the TaskDash default.
_notes.arcgis.service_tags: Comma-separated tags for a service that TaskDash creates; empty uses taskdash,monitoring,scheduled tasks.
_notes.arcgis.dashboard_tags: Comma-separated tags for the dashboard. Empty sets taskdash,monitoring when TaskDash creates it and keeps tags you edit later; a value here overwrites them at every rebuild.
_notes.alerting.enabled: Turn alert e-mails on or off.
_notes.alerting.healthcheck_url: Address pinged after each good run so an outside monitor sees a silent collector. Use one check for each computer.
_notes.alerting.include_log_tail: True puts the last lines of a failed task's log in the alert e-mail; false leaves them out.
_notes.alerting.dashboard_url: Dashboard link placed in alert e-mails.
_notes.alerting.heartbeat_hour: Hour of the day (0-23) for the daily check e-mail, which lists the problems still open. Not the dashboard's collector heartbeat tile.
_notes.alerting.realert_hours: Hours to wait before repeating an alert that has not cleared. 0 turns repeats off.
_notes.alerting.shared_cause_min_tasks: Number of failed tasks that makes one incident e-mail instead of one e-mail each. The e-mail names the cause when most of the tasks share it. 0 turns grouping off.
_notes.alerting.incident_digest_hours: Hours between reminder digests for an open incident.
_notes.alerting.maintenance_windows: List of {task, start, end, reason}: task is a regex, start and end are ISO times with an offset such as -05:00 or Z.
_notes.scheduler.task_name_regex: Only tasks whose name matches this regex are monitored; empty means all.
_notes.scheduler.task_path_regex: Only tasks whose folder path matches this regex are monitored; empty means all.
_notes.scheduler.action_regex: Only tasks whose action matches this regex are monitored; empty means all.
_notes.scheduler.exclude_task_name_regex: Tasks whose name matches this regex are skipped.
_notes.scheduler.include_disabled: Keep disabled tasks in the inventory.
_notes.scheduler.exclude_command_target_types: Command target type names, such as VBScript or PowerShellScript (not file extensions such as .vbs), whose tasks are skipped. Names are not case-sensitive.
_notes.scheduler.interactive_required_pattern: Text (not a regex) found in commands that need a signed-in session, such as ArcGIS Pro's Python under a Single Use or Named User licence; empty keeps that default, false turns the check off.
_notes.scheduler.collector_task_name: Name of the task that runs this collector, without its folder, used to judge a late collector. Must match install_task.ps1 -TaskName (default TaskDash Collector).
_notes.scheduler.overdue_grace_minutes: Minutes a task may run late before it is called overdue.
_notes.scheduler.heartbeat_ignore_after_days: Days. A computer with no collector run for this long is silent. The dashboard's collector heartbeat tile counts it as silent, and the lowest 7-day success tile leaves it out. Must be above 0.
_notes.history.max_events_per_run: Most scheduler events read in one run.
_notes.history.days_back: Days of scheduler history to read.
_notes.history.first_run_max_events: Most events read on the first run, when the history is empty.
_notes.metrics.days_back: Days of log files to mine for metrics.
_notes.metrics.max_log_files_per_task: Most log files read per task.
_notes.metrics.max_lines_per_file: Most lines read per log file.
_notes.metrics.log_directory_overrides: Object of full task name (folder and name, such as \Folder\Task) to log folder, for tasks whose logs the collector cannot find. The case does not matter.
_notes.metrics.log_roots: List of folders. When set, TaskDash reads logs only inside them. Empty reads any folder a task points at.
_notes.metrics.tasks: Object of full task name (folder and name, such as \Folder\Task; the case matters) to {enabled, prose_count_rules, noise_metric_key_patterns}.
_notes.upload.chunk_size: Rows sent to ArcGIS in each request.
_notes.retention.runs_days: Days to keep rows in the runs table.
_notes.retention.metrics_days: Days to keep rows in the metrics table.
_notes.retention.changes_days: Days to keep rows in the changes table.
_notes.logging.log_dir: Folder for the run logs; empty means the Logs folder next to the scripts.
_notes.smtp.port: Mail server port; 587 for STARTTLS, 465 for SSL.
_notes.smtp.user: Mail sign-in name; its password comes from the Windows keyring, never from this file.
_notes.smtp.ssl: Use SSL from the first byte. Leave null: SSL is on when smtp.port is 465, else off. Set true or false only to override.
_notes.smtp.allow_plaintext_auth: Set true only to send the mail password over an unencrypted connection.
_notes.privacy.hide_paths: Blank the script, working-folder and log paths and mask paths in setting notes and change summaries; paths inside command lines need hide_command_lines too.
_notes.arcgis.test_item_id: Development only; leave empty. Item ID of a test copy of that service, read by --target test.
_notes.arcgis.test_view_item_id: Development only; leave empty. Item ID of the read-only view on the test service.
_notes.alerting.mail_config_path: Deprecated. Path of an older mail settings file; leave empty and use the smtp block.
